correctness.rationale: For a d-simplex, barycentric facet coordinate λ_i and its opposite altitude give the supporting-hyperplane distance D_i=(d Vol(S)/A_i) λ_i. A volume-uniform point has Dirichlet(1,...,1) barycentrics E_i/sum E with independent Exp(1) E_i; ordered facet distances/ratios are therefore those of independent exponential clocks E_i/A_i of rates A_i. Competing-clock conditioning yields P(D_(2)/D_(1)>1+y)=H(y)=sum_i p_i/[1+(1-p_i)y], p_i=A_i/sum A. M_k=(-1)^k H^(k)(0+)/k!=sum_i p_i(1-p_i)^k recursively recovers power sums s_2..s_(d+1) from k=1..d, then Newton identities recover the unordered area profile including repeats. For triangles e2=M1/2, e3=(M2-M1/2)/3 gives the side-length cubic; SSS plus max p_i<1/2 characterizes nondegenerate triangle similarity/reflection. f_y(p)=p/[1+(1-p)y] has f_y''>0, so Jensen and strict Karamata on triangle profiles prove 3/(3+2y)<=H(y)<2/(2+y), sharp equilateral/degenerate limit. Exact rational p=(3,4,5)/12 gives e2=47/144 and e3=5/144, a local independent consistency check; source checker also uses finite Monte Carlo, not as proof.
